evals.prompt: /1-on-1-tutor-mode Michael Jackson. Goal: a solid overview of his life and why he mattered culturally, no deadline, I know basically nothing, standard depth. Plan it and show me the outline, then start.
evals.expected_output: An intake-free plan (the prompt already gives goal, deadline, prior knowledge, depth), a plan file at tutor-sessions/<slug>/plan.md with the fixed headings, a short outline of unit titles, and every reply ending with the Tutor Mode footer. The first teaching reply teaches exactly one concept with the foundation it needs, in as many plain sentences as that takes, with no filler sentence, and ends with a check question.
expectations: Every assistant reply ends with a line beginning 'Tutor Mode: ON'
A file matching tutor-sessions/*/plan.md exists and contains the headings '# Goal', '# Outline', '# Current Unit', '# Position', '# Learn Later', '# Misconceptions Caught', '# Session Log'
tutor-sessions/.active exists and contains the session slug
The outline reply lists unit titles one per line with no explanatory paragraphs
The first teaching reply introduces exactly one new concept, defines every term before using it, and ends with a question

No reply contains a praise opener, an announcing sentence such as 'this is the subtle part', an empty clause before a colon, an em-dash, or a slogan restating the point (node scripts/filler-lint.js on the reply reports nothing)

evals.prompt: We are in tutor mode on Michael Jackson, unit 1 (early life and the Jackson 5). The student says: 'got it. so when jackson won his rings with the bulls, was that before or after thriller?'
evals.expected_output: A blunt correction: the student has confused Michael Jordan with Michael Jackson. The reply names the confusion in its first sentence, gives the correct facts for both, returns to the current step, and carries the footer. No praise opener.
expectations: The reply mentions Michael Jordan by name and says the student confused the two
The reply does not contain 'great question', 'great observation', 'great connection', or 'you're right'
The reply returns to the current step of the current unit
The plan's '# Misconceptions Caught' section gains an entry
The reply ends with a 'Tutor Mode: ON' footer

evals.prompt: /1-on-1-tutor-mode evals/files/ I need to finish HW2 (evals/files/hw2.md) by tomorrow with real understanding. I know basic linear algebra. Standard depth. Plan it and show me the outline.
evals.expected_output: The plan's Materials table lists the lecture file as must-cover and the homework as the source of 'done when' tests. All four lecture topics (cones, affine sets, convex sets, separating hyperplanes) are units in the outline with slide ranges. Because the homework is due tomorrow and only needs convex sets and separating hyperplanes, those two come first and the cones and affine-sets units follow marked '(after deadline)'; nothing from the lecture is moved to Learn Later. The plan keeps the template's header fields and headings.
expectations: The plan's '# Materials' table names both files
The '# Outline' section contains units for cones, affine sets, convex sets, and separating hyperplanes; none of them is under '# Learn Later'
Convex sets comes before separating hyperplanes, and cones comes before affine sets (the lecture's relative order within each group)
Each outline unit line includes a 'done when' test and a source with slide numbers
The '# Goal' section records the deadline as tomorrow
node scripts/plan-lint.js on the plan reports no problems
The reply ends with a 'Tutor Mode: ON' footer

evals.prompt: We are in tutor mode on convex sets for HW2 due tomorrow, unit 3 of 5. The student says: 'wait, how does the simplex method actually pivot? like the tableau mechanics, go deep on that'
evals.expected_output: A rabbit-hole check: simplex pivoting is not needed for HW2, so the tutor reminds the student of the goal and deadline, offers to put it under Learn Later, and lets the student decide. If the student agrees, the plan's '# Learn Later' section gains a bullet with why and where it fits.
expectations: The reply mentions the goal or the deadline and offers to defer the topic
The reply does not start teaching simplex pivoting
The reply asks the student to decide
After the student says 'later', the plan's '# Learn Later' section contains a bullet mentioning simplex
The reply ends with a 'Tutor Mode: ON' footer

evals.prompt: We are in tutor mode on convex sets, unit 2 step 3. The student says: 'skip quizzes, i'm in a rush' and then 'where are we' and then 'exit tutor mode'.
evals.expected_output: The plan header switches to quizzes: off and the footer shows '· quizzes off'; 'where are we' gets three lines (goal, position, next) plus footer; the exit reply saves position and session log, deletes tutor-sessions/.active, tells how to resume, and has no footer.
expectations: After 'skip quizzes', the plan contains 'quizzes: off' and the footer contains 'quizzes off'
The 'where are we' reply is at most three lines of content plus the footer
After 'exit tutor mode', tutor-sessions/.active does not exist
The exit reply names the resume command '/1-on-1-tutor-mode resume <slug>'
The exit reply has no 'Tutor Mode: ON' footer

evals.prompt: We are in tutor mode on Michael Jackson, unit 1 of 9, step 2, pace default. The student says: 'this is too slow, just explain it, cover more at once'
evals.expected_output: The plan's pace field becomes dense, confirmed in one sentence, and the reply then teaches several steps of the current unit in one pass as continuous prose rather than one concept. It stops at the unit boundary at the latest, ends with a single check for the whole reply rather than one per idea, and carries the footer. The plan marks every step the reply covered and moves '# Position' to the last one.
expectations: The plan contains 'pace: dense'
The reply introduces more than one new concept, in dependency order
The reply ends with one check, not a check after each concept
The reply does not cross into a later unit than the current one
The plan's '# Current Unit' marks every step the reply covered as [x] and '# Position' names the last of them
Every term is still defined before it is used and the reply contains no filler
The reply ends with a 'Tutor Mode: ON' footer
